sources.title: PEP 354 alternative design distinctions
sources.sections_read: Rejected design headings: enumeration container and values; metaclass; linked values; hidden attributes
sources.confirmed: The document distinguishes the enum container from enumeration values and rejects conflating them. Its metaclass alternative creates an enum class and raises separate container-instance and singleton questions, so merely finding another language enum is not sufficient for either structural match.
sources.limits: This is a reread for item matching, not a new case or an additional minimum-count source. No baseline response is changed.

sources.title: RFC85 complete-match wrapper alternative: root boundary reread
sources.sections_read: Drawbacks / alternatives, whole-match input example and implementation/composability discussion
sources.confirmed: The fixed alternative wraps an entire match-like input containing new arm syntax; it explicitly discusses the need for a complicated procedural macro, unsuccessful declarative attempts, and weak composability. This gives a narrower matching question than merely generating any whole match expression.
sources.limits: Researcher match-boundary adjudication; an internal reviewer accepts a broader expansion-boundary match. Neither interpretation turns the later candidate into historical evidence. No implementation was run.

sources.title: Events redesign — linguistic structure boundary check
sources.sections_read: lines 68–72 and 375–380: sentence roles; stricter machine-readable structure alternative
sources.confirmed: The document maps active components and direct/indirect objects to event fields through an active-voice analogy. This is a concrete proposed structure, subsequently rejected because the authors prioritized human consumption; it is more than decorative terminology.
sources.limits: No external linguistic source is cited. The frozen primary coding treats this as a boundary internal schema design; counting it as other-field structure is a disclosed alternative definition, not a new primary gold label or an observed adoption benefit.
